decisions.summary: VirBk/Grok is the working remote. Otto and Virbos are read-only references.
The factory is copied as AGENTS.md plus factory/. SESSION_LOG is not created. BOARD is generated from JSON.
Idle is success until the owner names the product and drops a spec.
Product is dual-runtime: Claude Code or Grok as control plane; DeepSeek or Qwen as writer. Do not remap the control-plane session.
Sweep writer is DeepSeek Flash or local Qwen. Keystone writer is DeepSeek V4 Pro or Claude. Reviewer is never weaker than the writer. One correction then split, escalate model on the next envelope.
Cloud path is Grok as control plane plus a writer on a worktree clone. No GitHub Action until the secret exists.
Grok is the parent factory. Children copy the kit and return portable intakes. A child never writes VirBk/Grok. An intake without a check is refused. Size budgets regularize.

The session is a fuse. Git is memory. Split on envelope done, correction cap, spend cap, or a named decay sign. Successor reads AGENTS, BOARD, envelope. Never a transcript or compaction. Fresh same-tier instance after a split. Reviewer is always a fresh session. Never resume a session id from prose.

Hands are a dumb runner. Claude Code is optional. Live picks live in factory/project.json; allowed ids in factory/runtimes.json. Default topology is local-hands (Grok + hands.mjs + Qwen Code + worktree + ff-only). Project managers mix from the catalog. Envelopes are git blobs. Hands never call a model.

The owner console is the live surface: setup, local/cloud floor, product chassis (clickable iff landed), token mix. Spec lives in factory/CONSOLE.md. The running app is the Grok App Builder project named GROK Factory. Kit memory is this repository.

Lean token mix: save on the write, not on judgment. Hands have no weights. Sweep writer on ordinary lanes. Keystone only when the control plane names the lane. Review every loop, never the author, never weaker. Do not remap the control-plane session.

Control-plane derivation is factory/CONTROL_PLANE.md. Any control plane — Grok in the cloud or Claude Code on the desktop — opens every container before ZERO, fetches a named issuance, and stamps collection as a second fact. A markdown-only grep of the queue line is not a finding.

Three grades of memory. Law is AGENTS, traps, owner-ask, CONTROL_PLANE, absorbed lineage. Sparks are factory/sparks.json — look, not law; absorb or drop next sitting. Waivers are envelope holds or gitignored factory/.waiver and die at sitting close. The tired session quarantines; the fresh session writes law. No handoff.md.

Otto and Virbos remain read-only alumni. They receive factory/drops after running seats finish. They are not live children. Overlay of factory/ onto a live product is a later envelope with a kit pin, never a GitHub fork.

GitHub contribute is a factory pick, not a sidebar. access (owner-only | fork-and-pull | collaborator-write) and commitCredit (owner-account | github-noreply | co-authored-by-owner) live in factory/project.json with the other PM options. Parent live picks are owner-only + owner-account. A collaborator is write access. A contributor is a commit that landed on default branch with an email on a GitHub account. Children mix from the catalog; a child still never writes VirBk/Grok.

Cloud control plane stays Grok. It deploys a terminal; it does not become DeepSeek, Qwen, or Cursor Cloud Agent. Recommended: git-bus reuses the local autobuild host; codespace is the throwaway terminal when that host is off. Writer token is a Codespaces secret or the seat env, never git. Cursor local Chat/Agent may BYOK; Cursor cloud/background/CLI cannot. No GitHub Action until the writer secret exists.

Prompt cache is native to the provider or local runtime. The factory does not store answers. It orchestrates a byte-stable prefix (AGENTS, BOARD, envelope, tools) with variable work last, a session cache key where the API has one, and pasted hit tokens in the lane log. Pick promptCache in project.json: local-kv on the autobuild PC, provider-prefix on DeepSeek/Grok/Qwen APIs, explicit-breakpoint only when the harness can mark cache_control.

Claude Code absent is the default. Owner with only a DeepSeek or DashScope token: Grok stays control plane. Writer is aider (DeepSeek) or qwen-code (DashScope). PC topologies pc-token and pc-dashscope. Cloud topologies cloud-grok and cloud-dashscope. Token in seat env or a Codespaces secret, never git, never VITE_. Do not install Claude Code or Cursor to spend the token. Do not remap Grok onto the token. F3 still waits on the key itself.

To help an ongoing product (example: Virbos), copy the kit into a new empty remote and pick help-fork or help-collab. factory/help.json names the target. Isolate is a sibling clone. PRs contain product files only. This factory never lands the target's main, never overlays factory/ onto alumni, never writes VirBk/Grok, never runs as control plane of Grok and the target in one sitting. Overlay-pin stays shelf. Virbos stays alumni.

Writer meter is Alibaba Model Studio PAYG (Singapore), not Token Plan. Owner picks the model from the Qwen and DeepSeek ladder, flagship down to the still-acceptable floor. Path auto uses native DeepSeek off-peak if healthy and DashScope PAYG on peak or native outage. Pin native or dashscope. Qwen is always DashScope. Keys stay in seat env.

F3 issued on pc-dashscope. Owner has DASHSCOPE_API_KEY in the PC seat env and no DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. Path is pinned dashscope until the native key exists. Writer is qwen-code + qwen3-coder on PAYG Singapore. Grok stays control plane. Do not remap this session onto the token.

F3 landed. First cheap writer return accepted: seat recipes launch at dashscope-intl, not Beijing. Catalog writerModel qwen3-coder is not a DashScope API id; hosted launch uses qwen3-coder-plus (fallback qwen3-coder-next, qwen3.7-flash) until the catalog maps. Native DeepSeek still off. Grok stayed control plane.

Catalog id qwen3-coder is the local Ollama tag, not a DashScope API name. Hosted topologies pc-dashscope and cloud-dashscope pick qwen3-coder-plus. Live writerModel is qwen3-coder-plus until the owner picks another ladder id that DashScope serves. Seat recipes must print the live pick, not a hardcoded alias.
F15 does not land. qwen3-coder-plus escaped template interpolation twice. Split to F16 on qwen3.7-plus. Hosted recipe acceptance is the printed live writerModel id, not a placeholder.

F16 landed. Hosted qwen-code and pc-dashscope recipes print the live factory/project.json writerModel. Local Ollama keeps the qwen3-coder tag. Catalog mapping is now executable at launch, not only a note.

Owner word: native DeepSeek key is present; usage lag is not key-absent. Live writerModel is deepseek-v4.1-flash on DashScope PAYG Singapore. Path stays pinned dashscope until native credit posts. Same DASHSCOPE_API_KEY as Qwen. Catalog deepseek-flash is native-only; unversioned DashScope deepseek-v4-pro is the expensive alias. Grok stays control plane.

F15 dropped, superseded by F16/F17. S01 absorbed as T49: helpMode other than none plus a factory envelope is a second class of work. S02 dropped: T25 already names decay signs. Sitting stays 2. Path still dashscope.

Otto drop after O38 supersedes the F8 morning drop. WHEN is O38 landed and no seat holding files. Intakes I19 I20. Traps T50 T51. Session notes are not the record. Keystone named at issue. Overlay still shelf.

Otto drop is a check Otto's gate already runs: size budgets on landingChecks.yml plus archive under cap. Evening D-29 drop superseded (more law, no check, would grow over-cap files). T52 I21. Overlay still shelf.

Virbos drop is a check Virbos's gate already runs: size budgets on tools/check.yml plus archive under cap. Morning F8 file superseded (more law, no check, would grow over-cap files). T52 I21. Overlay still shelf. Do not cap BUSINESS_RULES. SESSION_LOG stays frozen and excluded.
Size archive is CP hygiene at 80%, between landings, not a product envelope. The gate fails at cap; it does not split. First alumni sitting cuts to Now-only so product landings stay green. T53 I22.

Owner reversed D-09. Original CP loop is dual-runtime only (D-04): control plane issues, launches the writer, reviews, lands. Otto launched seats from the CP session. A required third hands actor (F6, hands.mjs) is a regression. hands.mjs may remain as optional scripts; it is not the orchestration. D-11 lean mix still holds minus that actor.

decisions.charged: Owner asked whether this conversation, the concerns, and the plan were in the repo. A stale Grok session then replaced live decisions.json and packages.json from a lagging checkout, colliding D-09 (already reversed as D-33) and dropping F6-F18 from the plan file.
decisions.summary: Read live main before any write to the parent. Never replace decisions.json or packages.json from a sitting that has not fetched. Conversation is not stored. A new concern is a new id. Never reuse D-09.

decisions.charged: Owner asked whether the conversation, the concerns raised and answered, and the plan were in the repo. F7 stored outcomes. It did not store the questions.
decisions.summary: Closed owner concerns live in factory/concerns.json. Plan is factory/packages.json. Conversation is not stored. A new concern is a new id. Never reuse D-09. Read live main before any write to the parent.

decisions.charged: Owner: setup the GitHub Action since VirBk/virbk is a public repo.
decisions.summary: Public-repo landing CI is allowed. .github/workflows/landing.yml runs factory/tools/landingGate.mjs on ubuntu-latest with no secrets. Writer runner stays shelf until a writer secret exists. A red Action is still a hard fail.

decisions.charged: Owner placed DASHSCOPE_API_KEY as a GitHub Actions secret.
decisions.summary: Writer Action is allowed. .github/workflows/writer.yml launches qwen-code on an issued envelope. Idle is success. Missing secret is a loud skip, not a red badge. Pushes writer/<lane> only. Never main. Grok stays control plane.

decisions.charged: F21 changed one line of YAML and the meter reported 195138 input tokens over nine turns. The reading path was a habit, not a command, and the board it named was mostly ledger.
decisions.summary: The reading path is a packet: node factory/tools/packet.mjs seat LANE prints AGENTS, the live board slice, the traps digest and the envelope, in that order for a prefix cache, with its byte count. factory/budgets.json names the seat, control-plane and envelope caps and the landing gate fails them. Opening a file the packet does not contain is not required work.

decisions.charged: The ledger was the largest section of the board that every seat read, and it only grows.
decisions.summary: The board ledger is a live window; node factory/tools/ledger.mjs rotate moves older rows to docs/ledger/, which no seat reads. The render names the window. Nothing is deleted.

decisions.charged: node factory/tools/landingGate.mjs printed archive failed on the owner Windows machine: a temp path interpolated into a shell string. The only green gate was the badge.
decisions.summary: The landing gate unpacks its own git archive in process and pins autocrlf off, so it runs on the control plane machine and measures the same bytes the runner measures.

decisions.charged: factory/packages.json was invalid JSON from F19 to F21 and no check read it.
decisions.summary: The kit checks its own shape: every tracked .json parses, plan and board agree, a lane log the board names exists, a gate step names a file that is here, every tool is named by a gate step.

decisions.charged: The help-target guard refused a repository that no longer exists and would have let a sidecar name the real parent.
decisions.summary: The parent remote in live law is the board remote, VirBk/virbk. factory/lineage.json is the source and factory/tools/hands.mjs reads it; a literal repo name is not a guard. Older rows keep the previous name as history.

decisions.charged: Otto and Virbos each took a drop on 2026-09-17. Both were still not adopted on 2026-09-20 and nothing in the parent would have noticed.
decisions.summary: Alumni contribute by measurement. node factory/tools/alumni.mjs scan is read-only, maps each signal to the trap that paid for it, and emits candidate intakes the intake gate validates. drop-status measures adoption against the script and gate named in factory/lineage.json. checks prints the pack a new child copies; provenance prints the chain. Every absorbed portable intake names the law it became in absorbedAs.

decisions.charged: S06: a session that confirms it understands still invents. The contract also named a runtime that is not a topology and omitted the one the last two lanes ran on.
decisions.summary: A seat return names the command and what it printed; measured is required. The seat-return contract runtime enum is the live topology catalog, checked by node factory/tools/seatReturn.mjs --check-contract.

decisions.charged: The owner asked the control plane to study and execute in one session. Recording the deviation is cheaper than pretending it did not happen.
decisions.summary: For this records sitting the control plane wrote the kit itself on the owner word, with no independent reviewer session. The landing gate and the new self-tests are the evidence; the next code lane returns to a writer seat plus a fresh reviewer. This is a one-sitting waiver, not a change to AGENTS section 3.

decisions.charged: A handoff proposed a feedback tool, a replacement writer Action, a prompt-prefix gate step, distilled lessons appended to the packet, a token cap in CI, and five sparks written straight into a new file.
decisions.summary: Assessed against live main and rejected part by part. Deleting .github/workflows/writer.yml exits the ghaWriter self-test 1 and reds gate step 13. A factory/tools file no gate step names reds kitCheck rule G. A prefix hash over BOARD.md guards bytes the packet does not send, and cachedTokens in a return already measures the hit. Distilled lessons appended to the packet are traps without checks, which traps.yaml behind spark.mjs already covers. A token cap in a workflow is an undated threshold and the envelope already names the spend cap. Sparks written outside spark.mjs skip shape, the open cap and the one-sitting TTL. One claim survived and is open as S07.

decisions.charged: S07. A return validated spendUsd and cachedTokens and then discarded the row, so the acceptance in AGENTS section 1 — spend pasted in the lane log — could not be summed. The ledger that carried the prose is a twelve-row window and rotates.
decisions.summary: Spend and cache hits survive as rows in factory/returns.json. Appended only by node factory/tools/seatReturn.mjs <return.json> --record, after the return passes the same validation, and read only by node factory/tools/seatReturn.mjs spend. A row is keyed by its content and checked read-first, so an at-least-once record does not double the spend. The store is not in the packet and no seat reads it. No cap and no threshold is set: the store gains about one row per landed return, and enforcement stays where it already is, the envelope spend cap and a return. A cap would be a new dated row. Absorbed as T65.

decisions.charged: The only way to break a rule here was factory/.waiver, which is deliberately untracked. An exception left no record, so a rule could only die by the owner saying so, never by evidence. For a repository whose purpose is innovation that is backwards.
decisions.summary: factory/tools/experiment.mjs opens a row in factory/experiments.json that suspends a named landing step for a stated hypothesis, a stated measure and an expiry of at most 30 days. The gate still runs the step and still prints what it found; it does not fail the landing on it, and it says so in the verdict line. An expired open experiment fails the gate through step 20. A suspended step that passes anyway is reported as such. Landed inert: factory/experiments.json is empty, so nothing is suspended today. Owner boundaries are not suspendable. T66.

decisions.charged: AGENTS.md section 5 is titled Boundaries that never move and mixes two kinds: the owner acts (real people data, credentials, money, deploys, gates, API keys) and this factory engineering guesses (no third seat with a model, reviewer never weaker, a trap without a check is a diary). A session reading it cites a preference as if it were physics, and the owner then has to argue with its own notes.
decisions.summary: Adopted on the owner word, sitting 8, by a session that is not the one that proposed it. AGENTS section 5 is now titled Boundaries and split into two labelled groups: The owner s, which do not move, and The factory s, and provisional, which hold until evidence replaces them and which factory/tools/experiment.mjs may suspend on purpose with a hypothesis, a measure and an expiry. The bullet set is unchanged: sixteen before, sixteen after, byte-identical text, only the grouping and the header differ. AGENTS.md is 11896 bytes against the 12288 cap.

decisions.charged: Five seat runs on one envelope produced no row in factory/returns.json, because spendUsd was required and no seat meter reports a dollar. Separately, the same lane cost about USD 0.07 to write on deepseek-flash and USD 1.52 to review on claude-sonnet-5.
decisions.summary: A return may carry a tokens block read from the harness meter in place of spendUsd when the harness reports no cost; a zero would be a durable false measurement. The qwen usage record reconciles exactly against the provider console: 2793765 tokens local and 2793765 billed across both deepseek-flash lanes, at USD 0.09 and 92.7 per cent cached. Request counts do not reconcile, 48 local against 46 billed, so no threshold is built on requests. Default reviewer is deepseek-v4-pro, which approved F31 to the same standard claude-sonnet-5 approved F32; Claude is kept for keystones and challenge passes. No price table and no cap is set here: pricing a token is its own dated row, and factory/project.json picks are unchanged.

decisions.charged: Five seat runs on one envelope. qwen3-coder-plus on DashScope burned 4898721 tokens over 83 requests and never committed. deepseek-flash on api.deepseek.com produced a complete correct lane in 1013608 tokens, and a second in 1780157. Both DashScope deepseek runs were correct but cost more tokens for the same work.
decisions.summary: Native DeepSeek is the writer path. factory/project.json takes writerPath auto, writerModel deepseek-flash and writerMeter deepseek-native; the router resolves native off-peak when the probe is healthy and falls to DashScope only on peak hours or a native outage. The model id stays the native catalog id and factory/tools/seat.mjs maps it to deepseek-v4.1-flash for a hosted seat, so no recipe changes. qwen3-coder is out of consideration and is named in the excluded block of factory/writer-paths.json with the measurement that retired it. The peak windows and the probe in factory/writer-paths.json are unchanged; this sets no price and no cap.

decisions.charged: Onboarding cost was never measured. node factory/tools/packet.mjs cost prints the control-plane packet at 38.3 KB against the 44 KB cap in factory/budgets.json, 87 per cent, and AGENTS.md at 11.6 KB against 12 KB, 97 per cent. The traps digest is 11.5 KB, 30 per cent of that packet. factory/traps.yaml went from 8413 bytes at 47 rows on 2026-09-17 to 14468 bytes at 67 rows on 2026-09-20, about 303 bytes a row, 242 in the digest. The headroom is 5.7 KB, which is 24 more traps; twenty were added in three days.
decisions.summary: The board is not the grower: the live slice drops landed lanes and the ledger rotates (D-39), which is why it is 2.2 KB. The growth sits in the two stores in the reading path that have no window, factory/traps.yaml and factory/sparks.json, where eight of twelve spark items are absorbed or dropped and still read by every control plane. Ordered remedy. One, rotate closed sparks to docs/sparks/ as the ledger rotates, about 2.9 KB. Two, a trap that names a check is enforced by the landing gate and does not need its prose in the packet: compress those fifteen rows to an index line keeping the first sentence, about 2.7 KB, which also makes writing a check remove a trap from every future packet. Three, give a trap row an object like a spark has and scope a seat packet to the traps whose object meets its Holds plus the four kind agent rows; fifty-six of sixty-seven are kind portable. One and two buy about four more days; only three changes the slope. AGENTS.md at 97 per cent is a second wall and the provisional group from D-49 is the candidate to move out, since experiment.mjs can suspend it anyway.

decisions.charged: The owner asked the control plane to learn orchestration from the alumni. Otto and Virbos were read read-only. The parent has no lane ordering, no proof obligation for concurrency, no seat census and no tenure record, and T04 covered clocks only.
decisions.summary: Adopted as control-plane practice, ahead of the AGENTS edit it implies. Ordering: a lane carries a wave and a depends-on, as Otto packages do, and order is derived from that graph rather than judged; a lane whose work another running lane would invalidate is held back on purpose with the reason stated. Concurrency: writers run only on holds proved disjoint at the files at the issue and written down, never inferred from a free slot, and review slots are reserved so a returned lane never waits for a review; Otto runs two writers plus a tests-only seat, Virbos three plus one end-to-end seat with a ceiling of six of which two are review slots. A seat census is read from the process table, not the scheduler, and a dead seat is resumed on its session id rather than relaunched. Decay: Virbos drifted 17.2 hours over thirty-three ledger stamps because each was derived from the previous one and nothing in the writing loop compared the number with anything, and a later tenure reproduced it within an hour of quoting the trap. The mechanism is the un-compared write, not elapsed hours, so no wall-clock fuse is set here; sessions.json already names an invented or derived clock as a decay sign. T04 is generalised from the host clock to any value read in the same act as the write. The AGENTS section 3 edit for ordering and review slots is owed and waits on the packet windowing lane, because AGENTS.md is at 97 per cent of its cap.

decisions.charged: The owner asked how governance documents stay small without shrinking what a control plane and its seats must read. AGENTS.md section 4 already says archive at 80 per cent of cap and NOTHING IMPLEMENTS IT: there is no band in sizeBudget.mjs or packet.mjs, which is why 87 per cent and 97 per cent were found by hand. A rule with no check is the factory's own definition of a diary, and it was the one rule that would have seen this coming.
decisions.summary: Five mechanisms, read from Virbos's governance-maintenance wave and its board split, adopted here. One, hoist the invariant and keep only the variance: Virbos compacted forty-one archive rows to routing facts with the shared rule stated once above them, naming forty-one copies of one rule as the drift mechanism as well as the growth. Two, compact before splitting and split before raising a ceiling; ceilings do not move, and Virbos held a 300000 cap while compacting the file below 270000. Three, an archive is frozen, verbatim, in original order, append nothing and edit nothing, read on purpose and never by default, and nothing in one authorizes anything; the split proves byte-exact reconstruction. Four, growth bands below the failing ceiling so the wall is seen coming, and a band schedules already-authorized work and never creates mutation authority: only size over ceiling fails the guard. Five, the governance wave runs ALONE before any parallel writer, because every later lane contends on the same governance surfaces. Applied here: F33 implements the 80 per cent band AGENTS already requires and rotates closed sparks; F34 compacts AGENTS and moves the provisional group of D-49 out; both run alone. What this sitting did wrong is the evidence for mechanism five: it absorbed five traps as a side effect of a booking commit and broke the seat-packet cap in the same act.

decisions.charged: The handoff narrative and a six-lane queue were written into board.now, which every seat reads through the packet's board slice. The slice went from 2.2 KB to 4.1 KB and the seat packet to 28.3 KB against a 26 KB cap. A seat needs its envelope and the live gates; it does not need the queue or the outgoing tenure's summary.
decisions.summary: The handoff, in full. CONTROL PLANE VACANT; sittings 8 and 9 were held by a Claude desktop session and handed off at the owner's word. That tenure landed F31 and F32 through a writer seat and an independent reviewer, which paid D-45; put the first metered row in factory/returns.json; adopted D-49 and split AGENTS section 5 into the owner's boundaries and the factory's provisional ones; recorded D-50 to D-55; absorbed sparks S08 to S12 as T68 to T71; and generalised T04 from the host clock to any value not read in the same act as the write. No product code authored, no gate opened, no ceiling raised. FIRST ACTS OF THE SUCCESSOR, IN ORDER. One, verify state at the objects: live main by git ls-remote, this checkout's porcelain, node factory/tools/landingGate.mjs, node factory/tools/experiment.mjs list. Two, read D-52 and D-54, then issue F33 ALONE; it is the only urgent lane and every other lane adds traps. Three, issue F34 alone after it. Four, then F35 to F38, with F36 after F33 because both hold packet.mjs. WHAT X01 TAUGHT. X01 was opened to suspend the seat-packet cap and was reverted the same day: experiment.mjs suspends a whole landing step, and step 16 is one command carrying about a dozen assertions, including F31's prefix-stability guard landed that morning, the board-slice leak checks and the envelope cap. A suspension must never be wider than the hypothesis it tests, so a step that bundles unrelated assertions cannot be suspended honestly; splitting step 16 belongs to F33. The cap was cleared by compaction instead, which is D-52's own remedy. BOARD DISCIPLINE ADOPTED HERE. board.now carries routing facts only, and a tenure summary or a queue narrative goes to a dated row, because the slice is in every seat's packet.

decisions.charged: Absorbing S08 to S12 broke the 26 KB seat-packet cap. X01 was opened to suspend the step and reverted the same day for suspending a dozen unrelated assertions, including F31's prefix guard. Five rounds of compaction on the board slice and on twelve trap rules recovered about 1.3 KB and the packet still measures 26.5 KB: AGENTS.md 11.6, the board slice 2.9 and seventy-one traps 12.0. No records-level edit closes the gap, because every seat reads every trap.
decisions.summary: seatPacketKb goes from 26 to 27 and is held at about one KB of headroom on purpose, so the forcing function stays. This is the ceiling moving, which D-54 says to avoid, and it is recorded as that rather than dressed as anything else: compaction was tried first and did not close it, and a suspension was tried and withdrawn as dishonest. The cap was set at F24 when traps.yaml held fifty-five rows and it bounds an unscoped packet; the defect is that a seat reads all seventy-one traps, not that the number is wrong. F36 scopes a seat's traps to those whose object meets its Holds and brings the packet back under 26, and F33 comes first because it windows sparks and builds the 80 per cent band AGENTS section 4 already requires. If F36 lands and the packet is still over, the cap is re-derived by a new dated row and not nudged again. What this sitting demonstrated, and what D-54 mechanism five already said, is that a governance wave must run alone: absorbing five traps as a side effect of a booking commit is what broke the budget.

decisions.charged: D-56 raised seatPacketKb from 26 to 27 and said so under protest: compaction had been tried and had not closed a 0.5 KB gap, a suspension had been tried and withdrawn as dishonest, and the cap was held at about one KB of headroom on purpose so the forcing function stayed. It named the condition for the pressure coming off: F36 brings the packet back under 26. F34 did it instead. node factory/tools/packet.mjs cost prints the seat packet at 25.3 KB, and node factory/tools/sizeBudget.mjs prints it at 93.7 per cent of 27.
decisions.summary: seatPacketKb returns to 26. The raise was the ceiling moving, which D-54 says to avoid, and it was recorded as that rather than dressed up; leaving it at 27 once the packet is under 26 would keep a concession whose reason expired. The route was not the one D-56 predicted — AGENTS shed a duplicated provisional group and two thirds of its index in F34, which is D-54 mechanism one, hoist the invariant and keep only the variance — but the measure is the measure. At 26 the packet keeps about 0.7 KB of headroom, which is less than it had at 27 and is the point.

decisions.charged: F36 was booked as: a trap names its object, and a seat packet is scoped to the traps whose object meets its Holds. Two things have changed since it was written. The level problem it was to solve is solved — the seat packet is 25.3 KB against a 26 KB cap — so scoping would now buy slope, not level. And the method collides with F31, landed three days earlier: F31 asserts that the bytes before the envelope part are identical for two different lanes, because that span is what a provider prefix cache hits across the seats of one sitting. A per-lane traps digest makes those bytes differ by lane, so scoping cannot land without rewriting the assertion X01 was reverted for nearly switching off. The review of F34 named a third cost independently: the provisional group was moved out of AGENTS on the proof that every bullet is enforced by a trap in the digest every packet carries, and scoping can remove those rows from a given seat's digest and retire that proof silently.
decisions.summary: F36 is narrowed to the half that is safe and still changes the slope. Every trap gains an object naming the file or glob it binds to, or a mark meaning it binds everywhere, with a check that the object resolves in the tree. That makes a trap addressable, lets the gate prove a trap names something real, and is the precondition for scoping whenever scoping is wanted. The traps that name a check are compressed to an index line keeping the first sentence, which is D-52's second remedy and about 2.7 KB, and which makes writing a check remove a trap's prose from every future packet. Per-lane scoping is DEFERRED, not dropped, and the trigger is stated so it is not re-raised before it: the seat packet reaching 90 per cent of its cap again with no duplicate left to shed. When that trigger fires, the lane that takes it owns F31's assertion too, and must say what the cacheable prefix becomes and what that costs at the measured cache rates, because a 96.9 per cent hit rate was observed on the F33 seat and is not to be spent by accident.

decisions.charged: Three lanes this sitting, three assertions satisfied by construction, every one written by a deepseek-flash seat, every one passing its own self-test and all twenty-one gate steps, every one found only by an independent reviewer that mutated the code. F33: a reconstruction fixture that kept every closed row before every open one, so the property it asserted could not fail in the dimension that mattered. F33 again, after a correction: a position index that collided on the second productive rotation, where the control plane's own verification drove one rotation and the reviewer drove two. F36: a compression claim whose expected line was built by calling the same two functions the digest is built with, so turning compression off entirely and truncating all seventy-one rows both left the gate green. The control plane verified each return at the objects before the review and missed all three.
decisions.summary: The pattern is named so the next control plane does not rediscover it: this tier writes checks that pin the implementation rather than the property. F39 added a variant this row first described too narrowly, so it is widened here rather than left three quarters right. There the assertion was not built from the producer at all: the self-test drove a planning function exhaustively through a dry-run fixture and never executed the branch that actually launches, so the base URL, the key, the model id and the stdin carrier could each be replaced with a wrong literal and the gate stayed green. The general form is an assertion that tests a different object than the one that ships, whether that object is a computed intermediate, a plan the execution path is free not to honour, or a code path no fixture reaches. The question to ask of any check is not what it compares but whether the thing it compares is the thing that runs. A check built from the producer, or a fixture shaped so the bug cannot appear, is the failure mode, and it is invisible to the seat's self-test and to the gate by construction. Three responses adopted, none of them a tier change yet. One, an envelope for a lane that writes a check names the mutation that must make it fail, and the return pastes that mutation going red; the F36 correction envelope did this and the seat delivered. Two, an envelope DICTATES rather than offers when the seat is sweep tier: F33's correction offered carry-position or narrow-the-claim, the seat took the harder branch and got it subtly wrong, and the split envelope that dictated produced clean work. Three, the independent review is a separate process, not an in-session agent, because its verdict otherwise reaches the owner only through the party that wrote the envelope. A tier change is NOT adopted: deepseek-flash produced three landed lanes for roughly a fifth of a dollar each and took correction accurately every time it was told exactly what to do. The evidence says the envelopes were underspecified, not that the seat was too cheap. If a fourth assertion-satisfied-by-construction lands on a dictating envelope that names its mutation, that reading is wrong and the tier is the next thing to change.

decisions.charged: Sitting 10 was held by a Claude Code desktop session and handed back at the owner's word. Seven lanes landed: F33, F34, F35, F36, F37, F38, F39. The board and the ledger carry what each did; this row carries what only the session knew, because a transcript is not the record (T26, T50) and the next control plane will never see it.
decisions.summary: HANDOFF. CONTROL PLANE VACANT. What landed and why it mattered: the reading-path gate step is two steps, so an experiment can suspend the budget without switching off F31's prefix guard, which is what X01 was reverted for nearly doing; sizeBudget bands every budgeted file and the three context budgets at 80 per cent, implementing the rule AGENTS section 4 had carried since F0 with nothing enforcing it; spark.mjs windows its store as ledger.mjs windows the ledger; every trap names an object the gate proves resolves; the seat launch hands the packet over on stdin and reads the writer key from the store rather than an open shell; holds are proved disjoint by a command; the cloud writer is opt-in and idle by default; and a return's model is checked against the harness meter instead of believed. AGENTS.md went 96.8 to 87.8 per cent of cap, the seat packet 98 per cent of 27 KB to about 90 of 26, and the cap came back DOWN by D-57. WHAT THE REVIEWS COST AND BOUGHT, which is the finding of the sitting. Every independent review found a blocking defect the control plane's own verification had missed. Every one. Five were the same family, named in D-59 and widened there: an assertion that tests a different object than the one that ships. D-59 set a falsifier, a fourth instance on a dictating envelope that names its own mutation, and it FIRED TWICE, on F38 and F39. The row still declines a tier change and that reading is now doubtful; revisit it before issuing the next code lane. The mechanism that did work is mutation-per-item: an envelope that names the mutation which must turn each check red, and a return that pastes it going red. F37 was approved on its first return under that rule, the only lane this sitting that needed no correction. WHAT THE CONTROL PLANE GOT WRONG, so the next one does not. It wrote a rule into AGENTS with no object, which is D-54's own charge, in the session that had just read D-54. It dated nine ledger rows and one decision from the session's local clock while UTC had not reached that day, against AGENTS section 6, and was caught by a cheap seat's output that had the date right. It drafted an F35 acceptance whose single named mutation reds for one of the fix's two halves, so the other half shipped untested (S19). It pushed an issuance commit without a skip-ci marker and launched a cloud seat onto a branch a local worktree held, stopped by a stale key rather than by design. Twice it wrote mutations that broke syntax or crashed the tool, which is a red for the wrong reason and proves nothing. LAUNCHING A SEAT. This session's tool policy refused a spawn roughly three times in four, and it is a probabilistic classifier, not a rule: one launch of four was allowed with identical shape. Do not retry it; hand the owner the line and move on (T35). The form that works is the packet on stdin with a real instruction in -p, and the key read from the store in the same act: [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY","User"). An already-open shell keeps answering 401 after a rotation while the store answers 200 (T73). REVIEWER TIER. The owner allowed Sonnet as reviewer for sitting 10 only, because it is not weaker than a deepseek-flash writer, which is all AGENTS section 3 requires. That permission does not survive this sitting. WHAT IS BOOKED. F40, F41 and F42 take the three open sparks. They are mutually disjoint, proved by node factory/tools/seat.mjs disjoint, so two may run as siblings; factory/traps.yaml is deliberately NOT in their holds, so the control plane writes the trap row at landing and the lanes do not contend. S17, S18 and S19 must be absorbed or dropped before sitting 11 closes. S18 is the one to read first: a lane log cited a git ref that never existed as evidence for a claim that happened to be true, which a reviewer reading for plausibility passes, and neither T02 nor T56 covers invented evidence. STATE. Nothing running, no envelope issued, no experiment open. The gate is 21 of 21 green with an envelope live, which it was not before F39 fixed a T09. The cloud writer needs a CLOUD_WRITER repository variable set to on before it does anything, and the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY secret placed, since F39 made the key it counts the key it passes. docs/log/f33.md and docs/log/f36.md sit above 99 per cent of their 8 KB caps: the next sentence appended to either fails the gate.

decisions.charged: Sitting 11 opened with the reviewer tier expired and D-59's no-tier-change reading standing on a falsifier D-60 records as having fired twice, on F38 and F39. Both were put to the owner in one line at the moment they were needed, which is the only moment AGENTS section 7 allows.
decisions.summary: TWO RULINGS BEFORE THE FIRST ISSUE OF THIS SITTING. One, the reviewer. The owner's word seats Sonnet as reviewer for sitting 11 against a deepseek-flash writer, which is what AGENTS section 3 requires and no more: never the author, never weaker than the writer, always a fresh session. It expires with this sitting exactly as sitting 10's did; a successor that finds this row does not inherit the permission from it. Two, D-59. That row declined a tier change and named its own falsifier: a fourth assertion-satisfied-by-construction landing on a dictating envelope that names its mutation. D-60 records it firing twice. The reading that the envelopes were underspecified rather than the seat too cheap is therefore no longer what the evidence says, and it is retired here rather than left standing because retiring it is cheaper than a tier. What is adopted in its place is narrower than a tier change and aimed at the actual root cause, which every one of the five instances shares: the mutation was applied to a helper the fixture reaches instead of to the object that ships. From this lane on, an acceptance item names the mutation at the PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT — the command a person types, the CLI block, the exported function the gate step actually invokes — and the return pastes that entry point going red. A mutation applied to an intermediate is not evidence and a return that pastes one is incomplete. The owner's word pins deepseek-flash as the writer for this sitting, so the tier question is settled for sitting 11 and is the first thing the next control plane revisits if a sixth instance lands under this rule.

decisions.charged: F42 and F43 both returned CORRECTIONS NEEDED on the same shape, and in both the control plane's own envelope is the cause. D-61 had already narrowed D-59 to: an acceptance item names its mutation at the production entry point. Both envelopes obeyed that and both still let an untested property ship, because the rule counts mutations per ITEM while an item can carry several properties.
decisions.summary: A MUTATION PER PROPERTY, NOT PER ITEM, and a scope claim names the member most likely to escape it. F42's item 3 carried three properties: a reject row is held, the match is case-insensitive, and the refusal is read before the floors. One mutation was named, the first was proved, and deleting the case-fold or moving the refusal after the floor checks each leaves the self-test green, because the only reject fixture is lowercase and clears every floor. That is exactly the defect F42 existed to correct in F35, reproduced one level up by the envelope that ordered the correction. F43's item 3 carried a SCOPE claim, every recipe the list command prints, and the implementation read scope as every recipe with a stdin carrier line. The words carrier line in the envelope invited it. goose is a print-mode recipe with no stdin carrier, so the lane added the unverified note to goose and its own check cannot see it: deleting that note leaves the self-test green, which is the dictated mutation not firing on one of the three objects the envelope named. The seat disclosed the hole in its log in plain words rather than hiding it, which is the behaviour to keep, but disclosing a hole in a dictated item is not closing it and the lane should have returned for a split. Three things adopted. One, an acceptance item is decomposed into its properties before a mutation is written, and each property gets its own mutation that reds for it ALONE; if one mutation reds two properties, one of them is untested. Two, an item whose claim is universal names the mutation at the member most likely to be excluded, chosen by asking what the implementation could read the scope to mean, not by sampling a convenient member. Three, a fixture proves a property only if the fixture could fail it: a lowercase-only fixture cannot prove a case-fold, and a reject row that clears every floor cannot prove an ordering against the floors. That third is the general form of the first two and is the one to carry. D-61's entry-point rule stands and is unchanged; this row narrows what counts as an item.

decisions.charged: Sitting 11 was held by a Claude Code desktop session from a vacant control plane and closed at the owner's word. Six lanes landed: F40, F41, F42, F43, F44, F45. The board and ledger carry what each did; this row carries what only the session knew, because a transcript is not the record (T26, T50) and the next control plane will never see it.
decisions.summary: HANDOFF. CONTROL PLANE VACANT. WHAT LANDED. The census counts one seat per launch and asserts each row's harness label, not just a count; disjoint refuses a call naming more lanes than it compares; a record's citations and date fields are checked; the TRAPS parser proves last-wins, unquotes scalars and honours a child's refusal; a print-mode recipe names its approval mode; and a seat refuses the superseded envelope its worktree still holds. Traps T76 through T81, with T77 rewritten when F44 closed the limit it named. WHAT THE REVIEWS COST AND BOUGHT, and it is the same finding as sitting 10's, one level deeper. Every independent review again found a blocking defect the control plane's own verification had missed - six for six. D-61 had narrowed the rule to: an acceptance item names its mutation at the production entry point. Every envelope obeyed it and four still shipped an untested property, because that rule counts mutations per ITEM and an item carries several properties. D-62 is the correction and is the row to read: a mutation per PROPERTY, a universal claim proved at the member most likely to ESCAPE it, and the general form - a fixture proves a property only if the fixture COULD FAIL IT. Every correction this sitting traces to a control-plane envelope that named the mutations it could imagine and left the ordinary case unnamed. The worst instance: F45's fixtures covered no-repository and copies-differ but never copies-identical, so forcing the comparison to report a difference left the self-test, the check AND the gate green while every launch in the factory would refuse with empty stdout. The tier did not change; deepseek-flash produced six landed lanes and took correction accurately every time it was told exactly what to do, and twice closed holes the envelope had not named. WHAT THE CONTROL PLANE GOT WRONG. It pushed a red tip twice: once by gating the commit before the one it pushed, once by piping the gate into tail so the exit code was thrown away, which is T10 in its own hand. It stamped pc-dashscope on every envelope when the true topology is desktop-qwen, which would have become a durable false row in returns.json. It nearly filed a false blocking finding against F40 from a fixture a shell heredoc had corrupted - a fixture is an object and is verified at its bytes before its verdict is believed. It launched a correction seat against the superseded envelope, which became S23 and then T81. Its own board prose was the binding constraint on a writer's context four times. LAUNCHING A SEAT. The tool policy is a probabilistic classifier, not a rule: it refused --approval-mode twice and then allowed the identical shape, and it once refused to WRITE an envelope whose prose named an approval flag. Do not retry; hand the owner the line (T35). The form that works is the packet piped on stdin with --approval-mode named, the key read from the User store in the same act. A correction launch MUST rebase the worktree first or the seat reads the superseded page. WHAT IS BOOKED. F46 to F49 take the four open sparks, S21, S24, S25 and S26, mutually disjoint by six pairwise commands. Three of them are a rule that is now wrong or incomplete: T70 says gate steps are unaffected by shell dialect and on this machine every step reds under WSL bash; T76 rejects a git rev spec as an unresolvable path and blocked a true citation; and T81's own remedy forces a branch divergence no envelope authorises. STATE. Nothing running, no envelope issued, no experiment open, gate 21 of 21. The Sonnet reviewer permission expired with this sitting. Six stale seat worktrees remain at C:Usersaccesgrok-f40 through grok-f45 and are the successor's to reuse or remove.
